headline_marked: [[Alonso makes winning start with Chelsea]] as Rogers scores on debut in 3-2 victory over Fulham
headline: Alonso makes winning start with Chelsea as Rogers scores on debut in 3-2 victory over Fulham
summary: Xabi Alonso secured his first victory as Chelsea boss with a thrilling 3-2 win against Fulham. Debutant Morgan Rogers and Joao Pedro's early strike sealed the win in a pulsating west London derby.
details: Xabi Alonso began his Chelsea tenure with a 3-2 victory over Fulham on Monday. The win featured a debut goal from Morgan Rogers and a strike from Joao Pedro just 31 seconds into the match.

Alonso was appointed to revive Chelsea after their disappointing 10th-place finish in the Premier League last season. The former Real Madrid boss aims to prove himself after being sacked by the Spanish club.
Joao Pedro's opener in the first minute was followed by a blunder from Chelsea keeper Robert Sanchez, which allowed Josh King to score an equalizer for Fulham.
Morgan Rogers then restored Chelsea's lead on his debut. He recently became the most expensive British player in history following his £117 million move from Aston Villa.
Cole Palmer further extended Chelsea's advantage after half-time. The Blues then survived a frantic finale after Gonzalo Garcia bagged Fulham's second goal, following another mistake by Sanchez.

The match also saw a reunion on the touchline, with Alonso emerging victorious against new Fulham boss Alvaro Arbeloa. The two were former teammates for Real Madrid and Liverpool, and also played for Spain.

Rogers and Palmer, who are close friends, immediately gelled on the pitch, leading a dynamic attacking display. Rogers played on the left of Chelsea's three-man attack, with Palmer on the right and Pedro centrally.

Alonso's reign got off to a stunning start when Levi Colwill's header reached Palmer, who flicked a deft pass to Pedro. Pedro timed his run perfectly and clipped a composed finish past Fulham goalkeeper Bernd Leno.

However, Chelsea's goalkeeper Robert Sanchez, who had shaky performances last term, was at fault for Fulham's first equalizer in the 23rd minute. King's strike was close enough for Sanchez to save, but he allowed the ball to squirm into the net.

Despite being occasionally exposed at the back by Alonso's bold 3-4-3 formation, Chelsea attacked with poise. Rogers restored the visitors' lead in the 41st minute with a clinical finish from 10 yards, following a brilliant move started by Palmer.
Not to be outdone, Palmer scored Chelsea's third goal four minutes after half-time. Pedro's build-up allowed Palmer to burst into the Fulham area and plant a low shot past Leno from a tight angle.

Fulham reduced the deficit in the 54th minute thanks to another error by Sanchez. Timothy Castagne's shot was weakly pushed out by the keeper, and Garcia pounced to head in the rebound on his debut after signing from Real Madrid.

topic: us universities urge international students return
headline_marked: [[US universities urge international students to return]] before Sept 15 new immigration rules
headline: US universities urge international students to return before Sept 15 new immigration rules
summary: New federal immigration rules take effect on September 15, impacting F-1 and J-1 visa holders. Universities are advising students to return before this date to avoid being subject to the new fixed-term stay system, which could limit their duration of stay.
details: US universities are urging international students to return before September 15, when new federal immigration rules take effect. These changes could significantly impact F-1 and J-1 visa holders' conditions for staying in the US.

Under the new regulations, international students will be granted a specific period of authorized stay, replacing the previous "duration of status" system. This means students will receive an end date on their Form I-94 upon entry or re-entry.

Universities like Harvard, Columbia, Ohio State, Georgetown, George Washington, and the University of Chicago have issued warnings. They advise students planning international travel near the September 15 deadline to reconsider their plans.

Returning before the deadline may exempt students from the new fixed-term system. Columbia University specifically requested international students to return by September 8 to facilitate preparation and coordination.

The new system generally sets an initial maximum stay of four years, which could significantly affect students in longer programs like some doctoral or medical courses. Those needing more time will have to apply for an extension through USCIS.

Students already in the US by September 15 and maintaining their F-1 or J-1 status will generally fall under transitional rules. They will not immediately need to apply for a new period of authorized stay solely due to the rule change.

However, if a student leaves the US after September 15 and re-enters, they will be admitted under the new fixed-term system. This is why universities are strongly encouraging students to complete their travel before the specified date.
The Department of Homeland Security's (DHS) new policy has already faced challenges in federal court. Several higher education organizations and labor unions are opposing the changes.
